memory_candidates.content: The zotero-cli-cc `zot` binary resolved by $PATH via a Nix/home-manager profile can fail all subcommands with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'httpx' (import-time failure in zotero_cli_cc/cli.py's add-chain), while a separately-installed uv tool binary (~/.local/share/uv/tools/zotero-cli-cc/bin/zot) works correctly. Since zotero-write.sh resolves zot via `command -v`, a dispatch-scoped PATH prefix (PATH="$HOME/.local/share/uv/tools/zotero-cli-cc/bin:$PATH") routes around the defect without any script edit or Nix/home-manager change. Also: `zot`'s read commands (read/search) query local SQLite only, so an item created via the Web API is invisible to them until a desktop client syncs -- verification of a freshly-created Zotero item must use an authenticated Web-API GET, never zot read/search.

user_decision.question: specs/literature/1-s2.0-0168007289900328-main.pdf is a redundant duplicate download of Goldblatt 1989 -- the same paper already lives durably in the corpus at ~/Projects/Literature/sources/goldblatt_1989/. It is gitignored and untracked, so deleting it is not git-recoverable. Should it be deleted or left in place?
